title.en: Naive Bayes: counting, smoothing, and why it works
title.zh: 朴素贝叶斯：计数、平滑，以及它为什么管用

description.en: From argmax P(y|x) to the naive Bayes rule, estimation by counting, the zero-probability problem and smoothing (with Laplace as a Dirichlet prior), logs, the linear view and its limits.
description.zh: 从 argmax P(y|x) 推到朴素贝叶斯公式，计数估计，零概率问题与平滑（含拉普拉斯平滑作为狄利克雷先验），对数、线性视角及其局限。

name.zh: 推导朴素贝叶斯分类器

name.zh: 用计数（最大似然）估计先验与似然

name.en: Naive Bayes as a linear classifier; calibration vs ranking
name.zh: 朴素贝叶斯作为线性分类器；校准与排序

description.zh: 以为朴素贝叶斯要求特征彼此独立，而不是给定类别后独立

description.en: Treating the unnormalised scores after dropping P(x) as probabilities
description.zh: 把去掉 P(x) 之后未归一化的分数当成概率

description.en: Reading a zero count as an impossible event rather than a small sample
description.zh: 把零计数当成事件不可能，而不是样本太小

description.en: Thinking a Gaussian density value must be at most 1
description.zh: 以为高斯密度值必须不超过 1

title.en: The idea: classify by counting, and what counting needs
title.zh: 想法：靠计数来分类，以及计数需要什么

text.en: Given a new instance $\mathbf{x}$ (a bundle of feature values), which class $y$ is most likely? In probability language: pick $\hat y = \arg\max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$. Naive Bayes is the classifier you get when you estimate that probability in the most frugal way possible.
text.zh: 给一个新实例 $\mathbf{x}$（一组特征取值），哪个类别 $y$ 最可能？用概率的话说：取 $\hat y = \arg\max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$。朴素贝叶斯就是用最省的办法去估计这个概率得到的分类器。

text.en: The obvious way: look in the training data for instances **identical** to $\mathbf{x}$ and take the commonest class among them. The deck's three thought experiments show where this works and where it fails:
text.zh: 最直接的办法：在训练数据里找和 $\mathbf{x}$ **完全一样**的实例，取其中最多的类别。课件的三个小实验说明它什么时候行、什么时候不行：

rows.en: 8 identical rows say yes, 1 row says no
rows.zh: 8 行相同的都说 yes，1 行说 no

rows.en: the same attributes as the 8 rows
3 identical rows yes, 3 identical rows no
rows.zh: 3 行相同的 yes，3 行相同的 no

rows.en: a tie: yes and no equally likely
rows.zh: 平局：yes 和 no 一样可能

rows.en: no row matches the query at all
rows.zh: 没有任何一行和查询相同

rows.en: nothing to count: we must generalise from similar rows
rows.zh: 没得数：只能从相似的行去推广

text.en: The third case is the normal one. With $F$ attributes of $V$ values each and $C$ classes you would need to see every combination a few times, about $C\,V^F$ instances: for 20 binary attributes and 2 classes that is 2,097,152 (over two million); for 60 three-valued attributes and 4 classes about $10^{29}$. No data set is that big, so exact-match counting only works for instances we have already seen.
text.zh: 第三种才是常态。$F$ 个属性、每个 $V$ 个取值、$C$ 个类别，每种组合都要见到几次，大约需要 $C\,V^F$ 个实例：20 个二值属性、2 个类别就是 2,097,152（两百多万）；60 个三值属性、4 个类别大约 $10^{29}$。没有数据集有这么大，所以“找完全相同的”只对见过的实例有用。

text.en: Naive Bayes's answer: do not count whole instances, count **one attribute at a time** and combine. The price is one assumption, and the whole lesson is about what it buys, what it costs, and how to repair its worst side effect (zero probabilities).
text.zh: 朴素贝叶斯的办法：不数整个实例，而是**一次只数一个属性**，再把它们合起来。代价是一个假设；这一课讲它换来了什么、花掉了什么，以及怎么修补它最大的副作用（零概率）。

prompt.en: A problem has 30 binary attributes and 2 classes. About how many training instances does exact-match counting need (at least one per combination)?
prompt.zh: 一个问题有 30 个二值属性、2 个类别。“完全匹配”式计数至少要多少训练实例（每种组合至少一个）？

feedback.en: That counts the parameters of a model that treats attributes separately. Exact matching needs one instance per combination of values: $V^F$, not $V \times F$.
feedback.zh: 这是把属性分开处理时的参数个数。完全匹配要每种取值组合各一个，是 $V^F$，不是 $V \times F$。

label.en: $2 \times 2^{30} \approx 2 \times 10^9$
label.zh: $2 \times 2^{30} \approx 2 \times 10^9$

feedback.en: The number of combinations grows exponentially in the number of attributes, not as a square.
feedback.zh: 组合数随属性个数指数增长，不是平方。

explain.en: $C\,V^F = 2 \cdot 2^{30}$: every added attribute doubles the need. This is the curse that the independence assumption removes.
explain.zh: $C\,V^F = 2 \cdot 2^{30}$：每多一个属性，需求翻一倍。独立性假设要消灭的就是这个“维度灾难”。

title.en: From argmax P(y|x) to the naive Bayes rule
title.zh: 从 argmax P(y|x) 推到朴素贝叶斯公式

say.en: The goal: among the classes, pick the one with the highest probability **given what we observed**. The trouble is that $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$, a probability of a class given a whole bundle, cannot be counted (previous page).
say.zh: 目标：在所有类别里，选“在观察到 $\mathbf{x}$ 之后”概率最高的那个。麻烦是 $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$ 是“给定整个特征组合时类别的概率”，数不出来（上一页）。

say.en: Bayes' rule turns the question around: instead of *class given features*, we need *features given class* ($P(\mathbf{x} \mid y)$, the **likelihood**) and how common each class is ($P(y)$, the **prior**). Both are easier to count: fix the class, then look only at its instances.
say.zh: 贝叶斯公式把问题倒过来：不问“给定特征的类别”，而问“给定类别的特征”（$P(\mathbf{x} \mid y)$，**似然**）和各类别本身有多常见（$P(y)$，**先验**）。两者都好数：先固定类别，只看它的实例。

why.en: $P(\mathbf{x}\mid y)P(y) = P(\mathbf{x}, y) = P(y\mid \mathbf{x})P(\mathbf{x})$: the same joint probability written two ways. Divide by $P(\mathbf{x})$.
why.zh: $P(\mathbf{x}\mid y)P(y) = P(\mathbf{x}, y) = P(y\mid \mathbf{x})P(\mathbf{x})$：同一个联合概率的两种写法，两边除以 $P(\mathbf{x})$。

say.en: Drop the denominator. $P(\mathbf{x})$, the probability of the evidence, does not contain $y$: it is the same number for every class, so it cannot change which class wins. (The scores that remain are no longer probabilities; to get probabilities divide each score by their sum.)
say.zh: 去掉分母。$P(\mathbf{x})$（证据本身的概率）里没有 $y$：对每个类别都是同一个数，改变不了谁最大。（剩下的分数不再是概率；想要概率，把每个分数除以它们的和。）

lines.tex: P(\mathbf{x} \mid y) = \prod_{m=1}^{F} P(x_m \mid x_1, \dots, x_{m-1}, y)

say.en: Still infeasible: $P(x_1, \dots, x_F \mid y)$ needs the whole bundle. The chain rule of probability is always true and splits it into one factor per feature, but the factor for $x_m$ still conditions on **all earlier features** as well as on $y$.
say.zh: 还是不可行：$P(x_1, \dots, x_F \mid y)$ 要整个组合。概率的链式法则永远成立，能把它拆成每个特征一个因子，但 $x_m$ 的因子仍然要以**前面所有特征**和 $y$ 为条件。

lines.tex: P(x_m \mid x_1, \dots, x_{m-1}, y) \;\approx\; P(x_m \mid y)

say.en: The naive assumption, the only approximation in the whole derivation: **once the class is known, the other features tell us nothing more about $x_m$**. Features are conditionally independent given the class. Each factor shrinks to a small table: one attribute against the class.
say.zh: 朴素假设，整个推导里唯一的近似：**类别一旦已知，其他特征就不再提供关于 $x_m$ 的信息**。给定类别，特征条件独立。每个因子缩成一张小表：一个属性对着类别。

say.en: The naive Bayes classifier: for each class multiply its prior by one likelihood per observed feature value, and choose the class with the largest product.
say.zh: 朴素贝叶斯分类器：对每个类别，把它的先验乘上每个观察到的特征取值各一个似然，取乘积最大的类别。

intro.en: Four moves, one of them an approximation. Watch which one.
intro.zh: 四步，其中一步是近似。注意看是哪一步。

outro.en: Only the fifth line is an assumption; everything else is exact. Note also what the assumption does *not* say: features need not be independent of each other overall, only independent **given the class** (next page).
outro.zh: 只有第五行是假设，其余都是精确的。也要注意它**没有**说什么：特征整体上不必相互独立，只需要**给定类别**后独立（下一页）。

alt.en: Class y with arrows to features x1 ... xF; no arrows between features.
alt.zh: 类别 y 指向特征 x1 ... xF；特征之间没有箭头。

text.en: The picture is the assumption: the class is the only parent of every feature. If you know $y$, the features are separate coin flips. If you do not know $y$, they are linked *through* $y$: in spam mail, seeing \"prize\" makes \"winner\" likelier because both signal spam. Conditional independence kills exactly that link once $y$ is given.
text.zh: 这张图就是假设：类别是每个特征唯一的“父亲”。知道了 $y$，各特征就是互不相干的抛硬币；不知道 $y$，它们经由 $y$ 相连：垃圾邮件里看到 “prize” 会让 “winner” 更可能，因为两者都在暗示垃圾邮件。条件独立正好在给定 $y$ 后切断这条联系。

title.en: Exam wording: the step from the joint to the product
title.zh: 考试里的说法：从联合到乘积这一步

body.en: The step $P(x_1, \dots, x_F \mid y) = \prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$ **implies** that, within one class, knowing some features' values does not change the probability of another feature's value. It **buys** a model of $F$ small tables per class instead of one table with $V^F$ cells, so it can be estimated from little data. It **costs** accuracy of the probabilities when features are in fact correlated within a class.
body.zh: 从 $P(x_1, \dots, x_F \mid y)$ 到 $\prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$ 这一步，**意味着**：在同一类别内，知道某些特征的取值不会改变另一个特征取值的概率。它**换来**每个类别 $F$ 张小表，而不是一张有 $V^F$ 格的大表，所以少量数据就能估计。它**花掉**的是：特征在类内其实相关时，概率就不准了。

rows.zh: 2 个类别、20 个二值属性

text.en: The deck lists the other things naive Bayes assumes: the training instances are independent of each other, and the training and test data come from the **same distribution**. These are not specific to naive Bayes; most of the course assumes them.
text.zh: 课件还列出朴素贝叶斯的其他假设：训练实例彼此独立，训练与测试数据来自**同一个分布**。这些并不是朴素贝叶斯独有的，这门课里大多数方法都默认它们。

prompt.en: Which statement is the naive Bayes assumption?
prompt.zh: 哪一条才是朴素贝叶斯的假设？

label.en: All features are independent of each other, always
label.zh: 所有特征无条件地相互独立

feedback.en: That is marginal independence, a much stronger claim and usually false. Naive Bayes only needs independence **given the class**.
feedback.zh: 这是无条件（边缘）独立，强得多，通常是假的。朴素贝叶斯只要求**给定类别**后独立。

label.en: Given the class, features are independent of each other
label.zh: 给定类别，特征之间相互独立

label.en: The class does not depend on the features
label.zh: 类别不依赖于特征

feedback.en: Then classification would be pointless: the features are exactly what carry information about the class.
feedback.zh: 那分类就没意义了：特征正是承载类别信息的东西。

explain.en: Conditional independence given $y$: $P(x_1, x_2 \mid y) = P(x_1 \mid y)P(x_2 \mid y)$, while in general $P(x_1, x_2) \ne P(x_1)P(x_2)$.
explain.zh: 给定 $y$ 的条件独立：$P(x_1, x_2 \mid y) = P(x_1 \mid y)P(x_2 \mid y)$，而一般 $P(x_1, x_2) \ne P(x_1)P(x_2)$。

title.en: Why naive Bayes is a generative model
title.zh: 为什么朴素贝叶斯是生成式模型

text.en: Read the formula $P(y)\prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$ as a recipe for **making** an instance: first draw a class $y$ from the prior; then, given that class, draw each feature independently from its own table. That is the generative story. Multiplying out the recipe gives the **joint** distribution $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$ and classification is Bayes' rule on top.
text.zh: 把公式 $P(y)\prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$ 读成“造”一个实例的配方：先按先验抽一个类别 $y$；再在该类别下，让每个特征从自己的表里各自独立地抽。这就是生成故事。把配方乘起来得到的是**联合**分布 $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$，分类则是在它上面用一次贝叶斯公式。

head.zh: 判别式（逻辑回归、决策树、k-NN）

rows.zh: 描述每个类别长什么样

rows.en: usually more accurate with lots of data

text.en: Being generative is also why naive Bayes handles **missing values** gracefully: to ignore an unobserved feature, just leave its factor out of the product (summing it out of a model whose features are independent gives 1).
text.zh: 生成式还有一个好处：能自然处理**缺失值**。要忽略一个没观察到的特征，只需把它那一项从乘积里去掉（对特征相互独立的模型把它求和消去，得到的就是 1）。

title.en: Training: the parameters are counts
title.zh: 训练：参数就是计数

text.en: The model has two kinds of numbers, both read off the training table by counting ($n(\cdot)$ is the number of training instances that satisfy the condition inside):
text.zh: 模型里有两类数，都从训练表里数出来（$n(\cdot)$ 表示满足括号内条件的训练实例个数）：

blocks.tex: P(y = k) = \frac{n(y = k)}{N}, \qquad P(x_m = j \mid y = k) = \frac{n(x_m = j,\; y = k)}{n(y = k)}

items.en: **Prior** $P(y=k)$: the share of the training instances that have class $k$.
items.zh: **先验** $P(y=k)$：训练实例里类别为 $k$ 的占比。

items.en: **Likelihood** $P(x_m = j \mid y = k)$: among the instances of class $k$ only, the share whose feature $m$ equals $j$. The denominator is the class count, not $N$.
items.zh: **似然** $P(x_m = j \mid y = k)$：只在类别 $k$ 的实例里，特征 $m$ 取 $j$ 的占比。分母是该类别的个数，不是 $N$。

text.en: The distribution used for each factor depends on the attribute. The class prior is Bernoulli for 2 classes and categorical for $C$ classes. A feature given its class is Bernoulli (two values), categorical ($V$ values) or Gaussian (a number):
text.zh: 每个因子用什么分布，取决于属性。类别先验：2 类用伯努利，$C$ 类用类别分布（categorical）。给定类别的特征：伯努利（两个取值）、类别分布（$V$ 个取值）或高斯（连续数值）：

head.zh: 每个类别、每个特征的参数

text.en: Why are the relative frequencies the right values? Because they are the maximum likelihood estimates; the next derivation shows it, and the deck's own binomial spam example is the two-valued special case (20 spam out of 100 emails gives $\hat\theta = 0.2$).
text.zh: 为什么相对频率就是对的取值？因为它们是最大似然估计；下一页推导给出证明，课件里的二项垃圾邮件例子就是两个取值的特例（100 封里 20 封垃圾邮件，$\hat\theta = 0.2$）。

title.en: Deeper: why counting is maximum likelihood
title.zh: 深入：为什么计数就是最大似然

say.en: Under the naive Bayes model and independent instances, the log-likelihood of the training data is a **sum of separate terms**: one for the class prior, and one for each (feature, class) pair.
say.zh: 在朴素贝叶斯模型和实例独立的前提下，训练数据的对数似然是**一堆互不相干的项之和**：一项是类别先验，其余每个（特征，类别）一项。

say.en: Because the terms do not share parameters, we can maximise each alone. Take one: feature $m$ within class $k$. Among the $n = n(y=k)$ instances, value $j$ occurred $n_j$ times, and each occurrence contributes $\log p_j$. The constraint says the $p_j$ form a distribution.
say.zh: 各项不共享参数，所以可以逐项单独最大化。取其中一项：类别 $k$ 内的特征 $m$。在 $n = n(y=k)$ 个实例里，取值 $j$ 出现了 $n_j$ 次，每次贡献 $\log p_j$。约束说的是 $p_j$ 构成一个分布。

say.en: Handle the constraint with a Lagrange multiplier $\lambda$: add $\lambda$ times the constraint violation, then set all derivatives to zero.
say.zh: 用拉格朗日乘子 $\lambda$ 处理约束：加上 $\lambda$ 乘以约束的偏差，再令所有导数为零。

say.en: Derivative with respect to one $p_j$: only the $j$-th term of each sum depends on it.
say.zh: 对某个 $p_j$ 求导：两个和里只有第 $j$ 项含它。

say.en: So every $p_j$ is proportional to its count $n_j$. The remaining question is the proportionality constant.
say.zh: 所以每个 $p_j$ 都与它的计数 $n_j$ 成正比。剩下的是比例常数。

say.en: The probabilities must add to 1, and the counts add to $n$.
say.zh: 概率之和必须为 1，而计数之和是 $n$。

say.en: The maximum likelihood estimate is the relative frequency, exactly the recipe of the previous page. The class prior is the same derivation with the class counts: $\hat P(y=k) = n(y=k)/N$.
say.zh: 最大似然估计就是相对频率，正是上一页的做法。类别先验是同样的推导，只是用类别计数：$\hat P(y=k) = n(y=k)/N$。

intro.en: Counting feels obvious; here is why it is also optimal, so that the zero counts later can be understood as a flaw of *maximum likelihood*, not of arithmetic.
intro.zh: 计数看着理所当然；这里说明它为什么也是最优的，这样后面的零计数就能被理解为**最大似然**的毛病，而不是算术的毛病。

outro.en: A zero count gives $\hat p_j = 0$: maximum likelihood is certain that anything unseen is impossible. Keep that in mind for smoothing.
outro.zh: 计数为零就得到 $\hat p_j = 0$：最大似然断定没见过的东西不可能发生。带着这一点去看平滑。

title.en: The deck's example: flu or cold?
title.zh: 课件的例子：流感还是感冒？

text.en: In the formulas below, F stands for Flu and C for Cold. **Training** is counting. Priors: $P(\text{F}) = \frac{3}{5}$, $P(\text{C}) = \frac{2}{5}$. Likelihoods (each is a count in the class over the class count; Flu has 3 instances, Cold has 2):
text.zh: 下面的公式里，F 代表 Flu，C 代表 Cold。**训练**就是计数。先验：$P(\text{F}) = \frac{3}{5}$，$P(\text{C}) = \frac{2}{5}$。似然（每个都是类内计数除以类别个数；Flu 有 3 个实例，Cold 有 2 个）：

text.en: Two patients will walk in. Ann has a mild headache, mild cough, normal temperature and a sore throat; Bob has a severe headache, mild cough, high temperature and no sore throat.
text.zh: 来两位病人。Ann：头痛 mild、咳嗽 mild、体温 normal、喉痛 yes；Bob：头痛 severe、咳嗽 mild、体温 high、无喉痛。

title.en: Ann: multiply and compare
title.zh: Ann：相乘再比较

say.en: For Flu, take the prior and one likelihood per symptom of Ann. $P(\text{mild headache} \mid \text{F}) = 0$ because every Flu patient so far had a severe headache, so the whole product is 0.
say.zh: 对 Flu：取先验，再乘 Ann 每个症状的似然。$P(\text{mild 头痛} \mid \text{F}) = 0$，因为目前所有流感病人头痛都是 severe，整个乘积于是为 0。

say.en: For Cold: prior $\frac{2}{5}$; mild headache $\frac12$, mild cough $\frac12$, normal temperature $1$, sore $\frac12$. Multiply the five numbers.
say.zh: 对 Cold：先验 $\frac{2}{5}$；mild 头痛 $\frac12$、mild 咳嗽 $\frac12$、体温 normal $1$、喉痛 yes $\frac12$。五个数相乘。

say.en: The larger score wins: predict Cold. (Normalising, $P(\text{C} \mid \text{Ann}) = 0.05/(0 + 0.05) = 1$: naive Bayes is *certain*. Remember that when we discuss calibration.)
say.zh: 分数大的赢：预测 Cold。（归一化后 $P(\text{C} \mid \text{Ann}) = 0.05/(0 + 0.05) = 1$：朴素贝叶斯“百分之百确定”。讨论校准时记住这一点。）

outro.en: The prediction is right, but only one zero decided it. Now Bob.
outro.zh: 预测没问题，但决定它的只是一个零。再看 Bob。

title.en: Bob: when every score is zero
title.zh: Bob：当所有分数都是零

text.en: Bob: severe headache, mild cough, high temperature, no sore throat.
text.zh: Bob：头痛 severe、咳嗽 mild、体温 high、无喉痛。

text.en: Flu is killed by $P(\text{sore = no} \mid \text{F}) = 0$ (no Flu patient had *no* sore throat); Cold by two zeros (severe headache and high temperature were never seen in a Cold patient). Both scores are 0: the model cannot choose, although Bob's symptoms are plainly flu-like. This is the **zero-probability problem**: a single count of zero wipes out all the other (maybe very informative) factors.
text.zh: Flu 被 $P(\text{喉痛 = no} \mid \text{F}) = 0$ 一票否决（没有流感病人“没有喉痛”）；Cold 被两个零否决（感冒病人里从没见过头痛 severe 和体温 high）。两个分数都是 0：模型没法选，虽然 Bob 的症状明显像流感。这就是**零概率问题**：一个零计数就抹掉所有其他（可能很有信息量的）因子。

text.en: The cause is the maximum likelihood estimate: with only 3 Flu patients, \"never seen\" is really \"seen fewer than about 1 time in 3\", not \"impossible\". The fix has a name: **no event is impossible**. Give every unseen combination a small positive probability, and keep the other probabilities a valid distribution.
text.zh: 原因在最大似然估计：只有 3 个流感病人，“没见过”其实是“出现频率低于约三分之一”，而不是“不可能”。补救办法有个名字：**没有任何事件是不可能的**。给每个没见过的组合一个小的正概率，并保证其他概率仍然构成合法分布。

text.en: Epsilon smoothing: the quick patch
text.zh: ε 平滑：最快的补丁

text.en: Simplest repair: wherever a likelihood is $0$, put a tiny constant $\varepsilon$ instead. Redo Bob:
text.zh: 最简单的补法：凡是似然为 $0$ 的地方，换成一个很小的常数 $\varepsilon$。重算 Bob：

text.en: Flu has one $\varepsilon$, Cold has two. With $\varepsilon$ tiny, $\varepsilon^2 \ll \varepsilon$, so Flu wins: \"fewest $\varepsilon$'s wins\". That is sensible: Flu explains Bob's symptoms with one never-seen event, Cold needs two.
text.zh: Flu 里有一个 $\varepsilon$，Cold 里有两个。$\varepsilon$ 很小时 $\varepsilon^2 \ll \varepsilon$，所以 Flu 赢：“ε 最少的赢”。这很合理：Flu 只需要一个没见过的事件来解释 Bob 的症状，Cold 需要两个。

text.en: How small? Smaller than $1/N$, the smallest probability any observed event can have (one count out of $N$). Then an unseen event is always rated less likely than a seen one, and since $1 + \varepsilon \approx 1$ we need not renormalise the other probabilities.
text.zh: 多小？要小于 $1/N$，也就是任何见过的事件能有的最小概率（$N$ 个里一个）。这样没见过的事件总是比见过的更不可能；又因为 $1 + \varepsilon \approx 1$，其他概率不必重新归一化。

text.en: The weakness: ε is arbitrary and comparisons reduce to counting ε's, so two unseen events are no longer told apart by anything else. Laplace smoothing does it more carefully.
text.zh: 弱点：ε 是随意取的，比较退化成数 ε 的个数，两个没见过的事件之间再无别的区别。拉普拉斯平滑做得更细致。

prompt.en: With $N = 1000$ training instances, which $\varepsilon$ fits epsilon smoothing?
prompt.zh: $N = 1000$ 个训练实例时，ε 平滑该取哪个 $\varepsilon$？

label.en: $\varepsilon = 0.01$
label.zh: $\varepsilon = 0.01$

feedback.en: That is larger than $1/N = 0.001$: an event never seen would be rated *likelier* than one seen once.
feedback.zh: 这比 $1/N = 0.001$ 大：没见过的事件反而比见过一次的更可能。

label.en: $\varepsilon = 10^{-9}$
label.zh: $\varepsilon = 10^{-9}$

label.en: $\varepsilon = 0.5$
label.zh: $\varepsilon = 0.5$

feedback.en: Far too large: it would swamp the real probabilities.
feedback.zh: 太大了：会淹没真实的概率。

explain.en: $\varepsilon \ll 1/N$, so unseen events rank below everything seen.
explain.zh: $\varepsilon \ll 1/N$，没见过的事件排在所有见过的之后。

title.en: Laplace smoothing: add pseudocounts
title.zh: 拉普拉斯平滑：加伪计数

text.en: Better: pretend you saw every value $\alpha$ extra times (a **pseudocount**) before looking at the data. Add $\alpha$ to every count; to keep the probabilities summing to 1, add $\alpha V$ to the denominator, where $V$ is the number of values the feature can take:
text.zh: 更好的办法：假装在看数据之前，每个取值已经各见过 $\alpha$ 次（**伪计数**）。每个计数加 $\alpha$；为了让概率之和仍为 1，分母加 $\alpha V$，$V$ 是该特征能取的值的个数：

blocks.tex: P(x_m = j \mid y = k) = \frac{n(x_m = j,\, y = k) + \alpha}{n(y = k) + \alpha V}

text.en: $\alpha = 1$ is Laplace's add-one rule (every count goes up by one: 0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 2, so the order of counts is kept); a general $\alpha > 0$ is add-$\alpha$ (add-$k$) smoothing; $\alpha = 0$ is plain maximum likelihood. Headache given Flu, with $V = 3$ values and $\alpha = 1$:
text.zh: $\alpha = 1$ 是拉普拉斯的“加一”规则（每个计数加一：0 变 1，1 变 2，计数的大小顺序不变）；一般的 $\alpha > 0$ 叫加 $\alpha$（add-$k$）平滑；$\alpha = 0$ 就是普通最大似然。Flu 条件下的头痛，$V = 3$，$\alpha = 1$：

text.en: Check it sums to 1: $\frac46 + \frac16 + \frac16 = 1$. The big probability shrank ($1 \to \frac23$) and the zeros grew ($0 \to \frac16$): probability mass moved from what was seen to what was not.
text.zh: 验证和为 1：$\frac46 + \frac16 + \frac16 = 1$。大的概率缩小了（$1 \to \frac23$），零的变大了（$0 \to \frac16$）：概率质量从见过的挪到了没见过的。

items.en: **With few instances the change is drastic, with many it is small:** $\frac{3+1}{3+3}$ moves a lot from $\frac33$, but $\frac{3000+1}{3000+3}$ hardly moves from $1$.
items.zh: **实例少时变化剧烈，实例多时变化很小：**$\frac{3+1}{3+3}$ 离 $\frac33$ 很远，$\frac{3000+1}{3000+3}$ 几乎不动。

items.en: **Variance goes down:** one odd observation moves the estimate less.
items.zh: **方差下降：**一个异常观察对估计的影响变小。

items.en: **Bias goes up:** it is no longer the maximum likelihood estimate; with a large $\alpha$ all values tend towards equally likely ($1/V$), ignoring the data.
items.zh: **偏差上升：**它不再是最大似然估计；$\alpha$ 很大时所有取值趋向等可能（$1/V$），无视数据。

items.en: Priors $P(y)$ are not normally smoothed in the deck; there are other schemes (Good-Turing, Kneser-Ney) outside this subject.
items.zh: 课件里类别先验 $P(y)$ 一般不平滑；还有别的平滑方法（Good-Turing、Kneser-Ney），不在本课范围。

title.en: Bob again, with add-one smoothing
title.zh: Bob 再算一遍：加一平滑

say.en: Smooth each likelihood with $\alpha = 1$. Flu has 3 instances; headache has $V=3$ values, the other three attributes $V=2$. For example sore = no: $\frac{0+1}{3+2} = \frac15$. The prior stays $\frac35$.
say.zh: 每个似然都用 $\alpha = 1$ 平滑。Flu 有 3 个实例；头痛 $V=3$ 个取值，其他三个属性 $V=2$。例如喉痛 = no：$\frac{0+1}{3+2} = \frac15$。先验仍是 $\frac35$。

say.en: Multiply: a small but positive number.
say.zh: 相乘：一个小但为正的数。

say.en: Same for Cold (2 instances): severe headache $\frac{0+1}{2+3} = \frac15$, high temperature $\frac{0+1}{2+2} = \frac14$.
say.zh: Cold（2 个实例）同样处理：头痛 severe $\frac{0+1}{2+3} = \frac15$，体温 high $\frac{0+1}{2+2} = \frac14$。

say.en: Multiply.
say.zh: 相乘。

say.en: Flu's score is larger, so Bob is predicted to have the flu, as ε-smoothing also said. Unlike ε, the numbers now carry information from the counts.
say.zh: Flu 的分数更大，预测 Bob 得流感，与 ε 平滑的结论一致。不同的是，现在的数字里带有计数提供的信息。

outro.en: Normalised, $P(\text{F} \mid \text{Bob}) = 0.793$: still not 0 or 1, as a diagnosis from five patients should be.
outro.zh: 归一化后 $P(\text{F} \mid \text{Bob}) = 0.793$：不再是 0 或 1，五个病人得出的诊断本该如此。

title.en: Deeper: Laplace smoothing is a prior (MAP)
title.zh: 深入：拉普拉斯平滑就是先验（MAP）

say.en: Say before seeing data we believe the value probabilities $\mathbf{p} = (p_1, \dots, p_V)$ come from a **symmetric Dirichlet** with parameter $a$. The Dirichlet is the natural prior over a probability vector (the Beta distribution, for $V = 2$); $a = 1$ is flat, $a > 1$ prefers near-uniform vectors.
say.zh: 设在看数据之前，我们相信取值概率 $\mathbf{p} = (p_1, \dots, p_V)$ 来自参数为 $a$ 的**对称狄利克雷分布**。狄利克雷是概率向量的天然先验（$V = 2$ 时就是 Beta 分布）；$a = 1$ 是平的，$a > 1$ 偏好接近均匀的向量。

say.en: The likelihood of the counts is what we maximised before: $n_j$ occurrences of value $j$.
say.zh: 计数的似然就是之前最大化的那个：取值 $j$ 出现 $n_j$ 次。

say.en: Posterior = prior $\times$ likelihood: the exponents just add. The prior acts like $a - 1$ **imaginary** occurrences of each value, seen before the real data.
say.zh: 后验 = 先验 $\times$ 似然：指数直接相加。先验的作用就像在真实数据之前，每个取值已经“虚拟地”出现过 $a - 1$ 次。

say.en: MAP (maximum a posteriori) maximises the posterior instead of the likelihood. Same method as before: take logs, add the Lagrange term for $\sum_j p_j = 1$.
say.zh: MAP（最大后验）是最大化后验而不是似然。方法和之前一样：取对数，加上 $\sum_j p_j = 1$ 的拉格朗日项。

say.en: Setting $\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial p_j = 0$ gives $p_j$ proportional to $n_j + a - 1$; the constant $\lambda$ is the sum of these over $j$: $\sum_j n_j + V(a-1)$.
say.zh: 令 $\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial p_j = 0$ 得 $p_j$ 与 $n_j + a - 1$ 成正比；常数 $\lambda$ 是它们对 $j$ 的和：$\sum_j n_j + V(a-1)$。

say.en: This is **exactly add-$\alpha$ smoothing** with $\alpha = a - 1$. Laplace's add-one rule is the MAP estimate under a Dirichlet with $a = 2$, a mild prior that prefers probabilities away from 0 and 1. Smoothing is not a hack: it is Bayesian estimation with a prior.
say.zh: 这**正是**取 $\alpha = a - 1$ 的加 $\alpha$ 平滑。拉普拉斯的加一规则，就是 $a = 2$ 的狄利克雷先验下的 MAP 估计：一个温和的先验，偏好远离 0 和 1 的概率。平滑不是权宜之计，而是带先验的贝叶斯估计。

intro.en: Why add $\alpha$, and why $\alpha V$ underneath? Here is where it comes from.
intro.zh: 为什么是加 $\alpha$、分母为什么加 $\alpha V$？来源在这里。

outro.en: Two footnotes. (1) $\alpha = 0$ is $a = 1$, the flat prior: MAP then equals maximum likelihood. (2) Using the posterior **mean** instead of the mode gives $(n_j + a)/(n + aV)$; with $a = 1$ (flat prior) that is add-one, the version often called Laplace's rule of succession. Which one is \"Laplace\" differs between textbooks; in this subject, the formula above with $\alpha = 1$ is what you use.
outro.zh: 两点补充。(1) $\alpha = 0$ 即 $a = 1$，是平的先验：此时 MAP 等于最大似然。(2) 若用后验**均值**而非众数，得到 $(n_j + a)/(n + aV)$；取 $a = 1$（平的先验）就是加一，常被称作拉普拉斯的继承律。哪个叫“拉普拉斯”各教材说法不同；这门课里用上面的公式、$\alpha = 1$ 即可。

title.en: Numeric attributes: Gaussian naive Bayes
title.zh: 数值属性：高斯朴素贝叶斯

text.en: For a numeric feature there is no table of values to count. Instead, for each class $k$ and feature $m$ assume a bell curve and learn its two parameters from the training instances **of that class**:
text.zh: 数值特征没有“取值表”可数。于是对每个类别 $k$、每个特征 $m$ 假设一条钟形曲线，只用**该类别的**训练实例学它的两个参数：

text.en: Average the values; then average the squared distances from that mean and take the root. The deck divides by $n_k$ (the maximum likelihood estimate), not $n_k - 1$. Its example: headache scores of the three Flu patients are $0.8, 0.5, 0.9$, giving $\hat\mu = 0.73$ and $\hat\sigma = 0.17$.
text.zh: 先对取值求平均，再对到均值的距离平方求平均，开根号。课件除以 $n_k$（最大似然估计），不是 $n_k - 1$。例子：三位流感病人的头痛得分是 $0.8, 0.5, 0.9$，得 $\hat\mu = 0.73$，$\hat\sigma = 0.17$。

text.en: Prediction plugs the value into the Gaussian density, in place of the table lookup:
text.zh: 预测时把取值代进高斯密度，代替查表：

text.en: Example: headache score $0.8$. Flu has $\hat\mu = 0.733,\ \hat\sigma = 0.170$ and density 2.173; Cold (scores $0.0, 0.3$) has $\hat\mu = 0.15,\ \hat\sigma = 0.15$ and density 0.0002. Flu fits far better (ratio about 9769 to 1), before the other features and priors are multiplied in.
text.zh: 例：头痛得分 $0.8$。Flu 的 $\hat\mu = 0.733,\ \hat\sigma = 0.170$，密度 2.173；Cold（得分 $0.0, 0.3$）的 $\hat\mu = 0.15,\ \hat\sigma = 0.15$，密度 0.0002。Flu 拟合得好得多（约 9769 比 1），这还没乘上其他特征和先验。

title.en: A density is not a probability
title.zh: 密度不是概率

body.en: With a small $\sigma$ the density at the mean exceeds 1 (here 2.17). That is fine: densities integrate to 1, they need not be at most 1. Only the comparison between classes matters, and the factors still multiply.
body.zh: $\sigma$ 很小时，均值处的密度会大于 1（这里是 2.17）。这没问题：密度的积分为 1，不必不超过 1。重要的只是各类别之间的比较，各因子照样相乘。

text.en: "Smoothing" for continuous features
text.zh: 连续特征的“平滑”

text.en: There are no unseen values to worry about, since the density is defined everywhere. The remaining danger is **zero variance**: if all instances of a class share the same value, $\hat\sigma = 0$ and the density divides by zero. Two fixes: (1) ignore the feature (safe if it is constant across all classes, since then it is a constant factor; a loss if it is constant only in some classes); (2) add a small $\varepsilon$ to the spread, e.g. a small fraction of the largest variance ($10^{-9}$ in scikit-learn).
text.zh: 这里不用担心没见过的取值，因为密度处处有定义。剩下的危险是**方差为零**：某个类别的所有实例该特征取值相同，则 $\hat\sigma = 0$，密度出现除以零。两种办法：(1) 忽略该特征（如果它在所有类别里都是同一个常数，这没问题，因为它只是个常数因子；如果只在某些类别里为常数，就损失了信息）；(2) 给方差加一个很小的 $\varepsilon$，例如最大方差的一小部分（scikit-learn 用 $10^{-9}$）。

prompt.en: A Gaussian naive Bayes feature has density 3.2 for class A and 0.4 for class B (same priors, no other features). What follows?
prompt.zh: 高斯朴素贝叶斯的某特征在类别 A 的密度是 3.2，在类别 B 是 0.4（先验相同、无其他特征）。能得出什么？

label.en: Impossible: a probability cannot exceed 1
label.zh: 不可能：概率不能大于 1

feedback.en: It is a density, not a probability; density values above 1 are normal when $\sigma$ is small.
feedback.zh: 这是密度而不是概率；$\sigma$ 小时密度大于 1 很正常。

label.en: Predict A: its score is larger
label.zh: 预测 A：它的分数更大

label.en: Predict B, since 0.4 is closer to a valid probability
label.zh: 预测 B，因为 0.4 更像合法的概率

feedback.en: Classification compares the scores; nothing needs to be at most 1.
feedback.zh: 分类只比较分数，没有什么必须不超过 1。

explain.en: Densities are compared directly, just like the table probabilities.
explain.zh: 密度直接比较，和查表得到的概率一样。

chapter.en: Numeric attributes, logs, and the linear view
chapter.zh: 数值属性、对数与线性视角

title.en: Working in log space
title.zh: 在对数空间里算

text.en: A real text classifier multiplies thousands of numbers below 1. A product of 1000 factors of $10^{-3}$ is $10^{-3000}$, far below the smallest double-precision number (about $10^{-308}$): the computer returns exactly **0.0**, and every class ties at 0. This is **underflow**.
text.zh: 真实的文本分类器要把几千个小于 1 的数相乘。1000 个 $10^{-3}$ 的乘积是 $10^{-3000}$，远小于双精度能表示的最小数（约 $10^{-308}$）：计算机直接返回 **0.0**，所有类别平手于 0。这就是**下溢**。

text.en: The log turns the product into a sum, and since $\log$ is increasing, the winning class does not change:
text.zh: 取对数把乘积变成和；又因为 $\log$ 是递增函数，赢家不变：

text.en: The same 1000 factors now give $1000 \ln 10^{-3} = -6907.8$, an ordinary number.

items.en: Log scores are **negative** (logs of probabilities $\le 1$); the **larger** (closer to 0) wins. Ann's Cold score $0.05$ is $\ln 0.05 = -2.9957$.
items.zh: 对数分数是**负数**（概率 $\le 1$ 的对数）；**越大**（越接近 0）越好。Ann 的 Cold 分数 $0.05$ 是 $\ln 0.05 = -2.9957$。

items.en: $\log 0$ is $-\infty$: an unsmoothed zero still breaks the computation, so smoothing is needed in log space too.
items.zh: $\log 0 = -\infty$：没平滑的零照样会毁掉计算，所以对数空间里也需要平滑。

items.en: Any base works as long as it is the same everywhere; the exam suggests practising logs on your calculator.
items.zh: 底数任意，只要全程一致；考试前建议用计算器练习对数。

prompt.en: Why is it valid to compare log scores instead of the products?
prompt.zh: 为什么可以比较对数分数而不是乘积？

label.en: Because the logs of the probabilities add up to 1
label.zh: 因为概率的对数加起来等于 1

feedback.en: Nothing of the sort: log scores are negative numbers; probabilities, not logs, sum to 1.
feedback.zh: 没这回事：对数分数是负数；和为 1 的是概率，不是对数。

label.en: Because the log is a strictly increasing function, so it preserves which score is largest
label.zh: 因为对数是严格递增函数，不会改变哪个分数最大

label.en: Because $\log P(\mathbf{x})$ cancels
label.zh: 因为 $\log P(\mathbf{x})$ 被约掉了

feedback.en: $P(\mathbf{x})$ was already dropped before taking logs; the validity here comes from monotonicity.
feedback.zh: $P(\mathbf{x})$ 在取对数之前就已经去掉了；这里成立靠的是单调性。

explain.en: $a < b \iff \log a < \log b$, so $\arg\max$ is unchanged.
explain.zh: $a < b \iff \log a < \log b$，所以 $\arg\max$ 不变。

title.en: Deeper: the decision rule is linear in log space
title.zh: 深入：决策规则在对数空间里是线性的

say.en: Take two classes and compare them by the **log-odds**: positive means class 1. The evidence $P(\mathbf{x})$ cancels in the ratio, and the naive product turns into a sum of per-feature log ratios.
say.zh: 取两个类别，用**对数几率**来比较：为正就是类别 1。证据 $P(\mathbf{x})$ 在比值里约掉，朴素乘积变成每个特征对数比的和。

say.en: Now let every feature be binary ($x_m \in \{0, 1\}$, e.g. a word is present or not), with $p_{m,k} = P(x_m = 1 \mid y = k)$. The exponent trick $p^{x}(1-p)^{1-x}$ picks $p$ when $x = 1$ and $1-p$ when $x = 0$.
say.zh: 现在让每个特征都是二值（$x_m \in \{0, 1\}$，例如某个词出现与否），记 $p_{m,k} = P(x_m = 1 \mid y = k)$。指数技巧 $p^{x}(1-p)^{1-x}$ 在 $x = 1$ 时取 $p$，在 $x = 0$ 时取 $1-p$。

say.en: Take the log of the ratio. Each feature's contribution is linear in its own value $x_m$, because $x_m$ sits in an exponent.
say.zh: 对比值取对数。每个特征的贡献都是它自己取值 $x_m$ 的线性函数，因为 $x_m$ 在指数位置上。

say.en: Collect the terms with $x_m$. The weight $w_m$ is the **log odds ratio** of the feature: how many log-units of evidence for class 1 the presence of feature $m$ adds. It is positive if the feature is likelier in class 1.
say.zh: 把含 $x_m$ 的项合并。权重 $w_m$ 是该特征的**对数优势比**：特征 $m$ 出现时给类别 1 增加多少对数单位的证据。该特征在类别 1 里更常见时为正。

lines.tex: \log\frac{P(1 \mid \mathbf{x})}{P(0 \mid \mathbf{x})} = b + \sum_{m} w_m x_m, \quad b = \log\frac{P(1)}{P(0)} + \sum_m \log\frac{1 - p_{m,1}}{1 - p_{m,0}}

say.en: Sum over features. The result is a bias $b$ plus a weighted sum of the features: a **linear function of $\mathbf{x}$**. The decision rule \"predict 1 if $b + \mathbf{w}^\top\mathbf{x} > 0$\" has a flat boundary (a hyperplane), like a perceptron or logistic regression.
say.zh: 对特征求和。结果是偏置 $b$ 加上特征的加权和：$\mathbf{x}$ 的**线性函数**。决策规则“若 $b + \mathbf{w}^\top\mathbf{x} > 0$ 则预测 1”的边界是平的（超平面），和感知机、逻辑回归一样。

say.en: Solve the log-odds for the probability: that is the logistic (sigmoid) function. So binary naive Bayes has **the same functional form as logistic regression**. The difference is how the weights are found: naive Bayes computes each $w_m$ from counts, one feature at a time (generative); logistic regression fits all weights together to maximise $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$ (discriminative).
say.zh: 把对数几率解成概率：就是逻辑（sigmoid）函数。所以二值朴素贝叶斯和**逻辑回归的函数形式相同**。区别在权重怎么得到：朴素贝叶斯用计数一个特征一个特征地算 $w_m$（生成式）；逻辑回归把所有权重放在一起去最大化 $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$（判别式）。

outro.en: With more than two classes the rule is $\arg\max_k \,(b_k + \mathbf{w}_k^\top\mathbf{x})$: still linear scores. (Gaussian naive Bayes is linear too when the classes share variances; with class-specific variances the boundary becomes quadratic.)
outro.zh: 多于两类时，规则是 $\arg\max_k \,(b_k + \mathbf{w}_k^\top\mathbf{x})$：仍是线性分数。（高斯朴素贝叶斯在各类方差相同时也是线性的；各类方差不同，边界变成二次曲线。）

title.en: Deeper: the weights by hand
title.zh: 深入：手算权重

text.en: A spam filter with two words. Prior $P(\text{spam}) = 0.4$. Word 1 appears in 80% of spam and 20% of ham; word 2 in 30% of spam and 60% of ham.
text.zh: 一个只有两个词的垃圾邮件过滤器。先验 $P(\text{spam}) = 0.4$。词 1 出现在 80% 的垃圾邮件和 20% 的正常邮件里；词 2 出现在 30% 的垃圾邮件和 60% 的正常邮件里。

text.en: Word 1 pushes strongly towards spam ($+2.77$), word 2 mildly towards ham ($-1.25$). An email containing only word 1 has log-odds $b + w_1 = 1.540$, i.e. $P(\text{spam}) = 0.824$; direct multiplication of the naive Bayes factors gives the same number (checked in code).
text.zh: 词 1 强烈指向垃圾邮件（$+2.77$），词 2 轻微指向正常邮件（$-1.25$）。只含词 1 的邮件，对数几率是 $b + w_1 = 1.540$，即 $P(\text{spam}) = 0.824$；把朴素贝叶斯的各因子直接相乘，得到同一个数（已在代码里核对）。

prompt.en: In $b + \sum_m w_m x_m$, what does a weight $w_m$ near 0 tell you about feature $m$?
prompt.zh: 在 $b + \sum_m w_m x_m$ 里，权重 $w_m$ 接近 0 说明特征 $m$ 怎样？

label.en: The feature is rare
label.zh: 该特征很少见

feedback.en: Rare features can still have a large $w_m$ (the ratio of its two class probabilities matters, not its size).
feedback.zh: 罕见的特征照样可以有很大的 $w_m$（起作用的是它在两类里概率的比值，而不是大小）。

label.en: The feature is about equally likely in both classes, so it carries no evidence
label.zh: 该特征在两个类里差不多一样常见，所以不提供证据

label.en: The feature always equals zero
label.zh: 该特征恒为 0

feedback.en: $w_m \approx 0$ says $p_{m,1} \approx p_{m,0}$; the feature may take either value often.
feedback.zh: $w_m \approx 0$ 说的是 $p_{m,1} \approx p_{m,0}$；该特征完全可以经常取两个值。

title.en: Deeper: a wrong model that still classifies well
title.zh: 深入：错误的模型为什么还能分得好

text.en: The deck calls the independence assumption \"nonsense\" and in the same breath says naive Bayes works surprisingly well. Both are true because of one distinction: **ranking the classes** versus **estimating the probabilities**.
text.zh: 课件说独立性假设是“胡说”，同时又说朴素贝叶斯出奇地好。两者都对，因为有一个区分：**给类别排序**与**估计概率**。

text.en: Suppose a word that signals spam (likelihood ratio 4 : 1, equal priors) appears in the email in $k$ perfectly correlated copies, for example the same word in several places, or several near-synonyms. Naive Bayes treats each copy as new evidence and multiplies the ratio $k$ times:
text.zh: 设一个指向垃圾邮件的词（似然比 4 : 1，先验相等）在邮件里有 $k$ 个完全相关的副本，比如同一个词出现多处，或几个近义词。朴素贝叶斯把每个副本都当成新证据，把比值乘 $k$ 次：

head.zh: 垃圾邮件几率（朴素贝叶斯）

text.en: The truth is odds of 4 (probability 0.80) whatever $k$ is. Naive Bayes gets the **direction** right (spam) but grows more and more **over-confident**: the probabilities are pushed towards 0 and 1, i.e. poorly **calibrated**. Classification only needs the sign of the log-odds, which is right as long as the errors do not overturn it; a decision threshold at 0 is robust to inflating the magnitude.
text.zh: 真实情况不论 $k$ 是多少，都是几率 4（概率 0.80）。朴素贝叶斯得到了正确的**方向**（垃圾邮件），但**越来越过度自信**：概率被推向 0 和 1，也就是**校准**很差。分类只需要对数几率的符号；只要误差没有把符号翻过来，它就是对的；阈值在 0 处的决策对“幅度被放大”很稳健。

items.en: **What can break it:** strongly correlated features that point in *different* directions can outvote the truth; the product then favours the wrong class. Redundant features are the main enemy; feature selection helps.
items.zh: **什么会让它失灵：**指向*不同*方向的强相关特征会把真相“投票”压倒，乘积偏向错误的类别。冗余特征是主要敌人，特征选择能帮忙。

items.en: **When you need probabilities** (expected costs, thresholds, combining with other models), do not trust naive Bayes's numbers directly: recalibrate (Platt scaling, isotonic regression) on held-out data. A ranking measure (AUC, accuracy) can look good while a probability measure (log loss, calibration curve) looks bad.
items.zh: **需要概率时**（期望代价、阈值、与别的模型组合），别直接信朴素贝叶斯给的数：在留出数据上重新校准（Platt 缩放、保序回归）。排序类指标（AUC、准确率）可能很好，概率类指标（对数损失、校准曲线）却很差。

items.en: Domingos and Pazzani (1997) showed naive Bayes can be optimal for 0-1 loss even with strong dependences: it needs only that the correct class gets the highest score, not that the scores are right. The deck's phrase: \"we do not need the true distribution over $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$, we just need to identify the most likely outcome.\"
items.zh: Domingos 与 Pazzani（1997）证明：即使有很强的依赖，朴素贝叶斯在 0-1 损失下也可能是最优的：它只需要正确类别得分最高，并不需要分数本身对。课件的说法：不需要真实的 $P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$，只需认出最可能的结果。

prompt.en: A naive Bayes spam filter reports $P(\text{spam}) = 0.999$ for 40% of the mails it flags, but only 80% of those are spam. What does this show?
prompt.zh: 一个朴素贝叶斯垃圾邮件过滤器，对它标记的邮件中 40% 报告 $P(\text{spam}) = 0.999$，但其中只有 80% 真的是垃圾邮件。这说明什么？

label.en: The model is poorly calibrated: its confidence is higher than its accuracy
label.zh: 模型校准差：它的自信超过了它的准确率

label.en: The classification is wrong for those mails
label.zh: 这些邮件的分类是错的

feedback.en: 80% correct is a good accuracy; the problem is the *stated* probability 0.999, not the decisions.
feedback.zh: 80% 正确是不错的准确率；问题出在*报告的*概率 0.999，不在决策。

label.en: Smoothing was set too low
label.zh: 平滑设得太小

feedback.en: Smoothing affects unseen events; this over-confidence comes from multiplying correlated evidence.
feedback.zh: 平滑影响的是没见过的事件；这里的过度自信来自把相关的证据连乘。

explain.en: Calibration compares stated probability with observed frequency; naive Bayes tends to say 0.999 when the truth is lower.
explain.zh: 校准比较的是报告的概率与实际频率；朴素贝叶斯常在真实概率更低时说 0.999。

title.en: Pros and cons
title.zh: 优点与缺点

rows.en: training is counting: one pass over the data, no iterations
rows.zh: 训练就是计数：扫一遍数据，不用迭代

rows.en: Scales to many features and data
rows.zh: 能扩展到大量特征和数据

rows.en: cost grows linearly in $F$ and $N$; the parameters are $F(V-1)$ per class, not $V^F$
rows.zh: 代价随 $F$ 和 $N$ 线性增长；参数是每类 $F(V-1)$ 个，不是 $V^F$

rows.en: each feature contributes one visible factor (or log-ratio weight)
rows.zh: 每个特征贡献一个看得见的因子（或对数比权重）

rows.en: leave the missing feature's factor out of the product
rows.zh: 把缺失特征的因子从乘积里去掉

rows.en: a fast baseline that works with little data
rows.zh: 快速的基线，数据少时也行
独立性假设通常不成立

rows.en: correlated features are counted twice; probabilities over-confident
rows.zh: 相关特征被重复计数；概率过度自信

rows.en: unseen (feature, class) pairs veto a class; needs smoothing
rows.zh: 没见过的（特征，类别）组合会一票否决某个类别；需要平滑

rows.en: the boundary is linear in log space; an XOR-like pattern is invisible to it
rows.zh: 边界在对数空间里是线性的；类似 XOR 的模式它看不见

rows.en: a non-Gaussian feature is fitted badly by a bell curve; discretising loses detail
rows.zh: 非高斯的特征被钟形曲线拟合得很差；离散化又损失细节

text.en: Compare with the neighbours in this course: k-NN keeps all data and needs no training but cannot scale in $F$; decision trees choose features and model interactions but fragment the data; naive Bayes is the cheapest and most data-frugal, at the price of the independence assumption.
text.zh: 和本课其他方法比：k-NN 保留所有数据、不用训练，但在 $F$ 上扩展不了；决策树能选特征、能建模交互，但会把数据切碎；朴素贝叶斯最便宜、最省数据，代价是独立性假设。

title.en: Check: which step is the approximation?
title.zh: 检查：哪一步是近似？

prompt.en: In the derivation $\hat y = \arg\max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x}) \to \arg\max_y P(y)P(\mathbf{x}\mid y) \to \arg\max_y P(y)\prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$, which step is an approximation and not an identity?
prompt.zh: 在推导 $\hat y = \arg\max_y P(y \mid \mathbf{x}) \to \arg\max_y P(y)P(\mathbf{x}\mid y) \to \arg\max_y P(y)\prod_m P(x_m \mid y)$ 中，哪一步是近似而不是恒等？

label.en: Applying Bayes' rule
label.zh: 用贝叶斯公式

feedback.en: Bayes' rule is exact: it just rewrites the same joint probability.
feedback.zh: 贝叶斯公式是精确的：只是把同一个联合概率换个写法。

label.en: Dropping $P(\mathbf{x})$
label.zh: 去掉 $P(\mathbf{x})$

feedback.en: Dropping the denominator does not change the $\arg\max$ because it is the same for every class; no approximation.
feedback.zh: 去掉分母不改变 $\arg\max$，因为它对每个类别相同；不是近似。

label.en: Replacing $P(\mathbf{x}\mid y)$ by the product of one-feature likelihoods
label.zh: 把 $P(\mathbf{x}\mid y)$ 换成单特征似然的乘积

explain.en: Only the conditional independence assumption is an approximation; the rest is exact.
explain.zh: 只有条件独立假设是近似；其余都是精确的。

title.en: Calculate: Laplace-smoothed score
title.zh: 计算：拉普拉斯平滑后的分数

prompt.en: Use the deck's five patients. Carl has a **mild** headache, **severe** cough, **normal** temperature and **sore = yes**. With Laplace smoothing ($\alpha = 1$) on every likelihood and the prior left as it is, what is the unnormalised score of **Flu**? Give a decimal to 4 places.
prompt.zh: 用课件里的五位病人。Carl：头痛 **mild**、咳嗽 **severe**、体温 **normal**、喉痛 **yes**。对所有似然用拉普拉斯平滑（$\alpha = 1$），先验不动，**Flu** 的未归一化分数是多少？写成小数，保留 4 位。

explain.en: Flu has 3 instances: headache mild $\frac{0+1}{3+3}$, cough severe $\frac{1+1}{3+2}$, temperature normal $\frac{2+1}{3+2}$, sore yes $\frac{3+1}{3+2}$; prior $\frac35$. Score $= \frac{12}{625} \approx 0.0192$.
explain.zh: Flu 有 3 个实例：头痛 mild $\frac{0+1}{3+3}$、咳嗽 severe $\frac{1+1}{3+2}$、体温 normal $\frac{2+1}{3+2}$、喉痛 yes $\frac{3+1}{3+2}$；先验 $\frac35$。分数 $= \frac{12}{625} \approx 0.0192$。

hints.en: Each attribute has its own $V$: headache 3, the others 2.
hints.zh: 每个属性有自己的 $V$：头痛 3，其他 2。

title.en: Calculate: from scores to a probability
title.zh: 计算：从分数到概率

prompt.en: For Carl (previous question), the Cold score under the same smoothing is $\frac{3}{100}$. Normalising the two scores, what is $P(\text{C} \mid \text{Carl})$? Three decimal places.
prompt.zh: 接上题，Carl 在同样平滑下的 Cold 分数是 $\frac{3}{100}$。把两个分数归一化，$P(\text{C} \mid \text{Carl})$ 是多少？保留三位小数。

explain.en: Divide by the sum of the scores: $\frac{\frac{3}{100}}{\frac{12}{625} + \frac{3}{100}} = 0.6098$. The dropped $P(\mathbf{x})$ is exactly this sum.
explain.zh: 除以分数之和：$\frac{\frac{3}{100}}{\frac{12}{625} + \frac{3}{100}} = 0.6098$。被去掉的 $P(\mathbf{x})$ 正是这个和。

title.en: Check: what smoothing does
title.zh: 检查：平滑做了什么

prompt.en: Compared with the maximum likelihood estimate, add-one smoothing on a small training set:
prompt.zh: 与最大似然估计相比，在小训练集上做加一平滑：

label.en: increases bias and reduces variance
label.zh: 增大偏差、减小方差

label.en: reduces bias, because it uses more information
label.zh: 减小偏差，因为用了更多信息

feedback.en: The pseudocounts are information that is **not** in the data; they pull the estimate away from the data's frequencies, which is bias.
feedback.zh: 伪计数是**不在**数据里的信息；它把估计从数据频率处拉开，这就是偏差。

label.en: leaves both unchanged but avoids zeros
label.zh: 两者都不变，只是避免零

feedback.en: Every estimate changes: the large probabilities shrink as the small ones grow. That is exactly a trade of variance for bias.
feedback.zh: 每个估计都变了：大的概率缩小，小的增大。这正是用方差换偏差。

explain.en: Smoothing is a prior: it adds bias, but makes the estimate less sensitive to individual observations.
explain.zh: 平滑就是先验：增加偏差，但让估计对个别观察不那么敏感。

title.en: Short answer: why does it work?
title.zh: 简答：为什么它还管用？

prompt.en: Naive Bayes assumes the features are conditionally independent given the class, which is almost never true. Explain in 2-3 lines why it often still classifies well, and what it does badly.
prompt.zh: 朴素贝叶斯假设特征在给定类别时条件独立，这几乎从不成立。用 2-3 行解释为什么它常常仍然分得好，以及它哪里做得不好。

key_points.en: Classification only needs the correct class to have the highest score, not correct probabilities
key_points.zh: Classification only needs the correct class to have the highest score, not correct probabilities

key_points.en: Correlated features are double counted, so probabilities are over-confident (poorly calibrated)
key_points.zh: Correlated features are double counted, so probabilities are over-confident (poorly calibrated)

key_points.en: Errors in the evidence often push all classes the same way, so the ranking survives
key_points.zh: Errors in the evidence often push all classes the same way, so the ranking survives

model_answer.en: Classification only needs the correct class to receive the largest score, not accurate probabilities. Correlated features are counted several times, which makes the posterior probabilities over-confident (poorly calibrated), but the errors often push all classes in the same direction, so the argmax is unchanged. It does badly when dependent features point to different classes, and its probability outputs should not be trusted without calibration.
model_answer.zh: Classification only needs the correct class to receive the largest score, not accurate probabilities. Correlated features are counted several times, which makes the posterior probabilities over-confident (poorly calibrated), but the errors often push all classes in the same direction, so the argmax is unchanged. It does badly when dependent features point to different classes, and its probability outputs should not be trusted without calibration.

explain.en: Name the distinction between ranking and calibration; mention double counting.
explain.zh: 要点是“排序”与“校准”的区别，以及重复计数。

title.en: Design question: a text classifier
title.zh: 设计题：文本分类器

prompt.en: You must build a naive Bayes classifier that labels support emails as *urgent* or *not urgent*, using the words in each email (50,000-word vocabulary, 2,000 labelled emails). Describe, in a few lines: what the model is, how its parameters are estimated, how you deal with words not seen in the training emails of one class, how you make the computation numerically safe, and one weakness you would watch for.
prompt.zh: 要用朴素贝叶斯把客服邮件分为*紧急*和*不紧急*，特征是邮件里的词（词表 5 万词，2000 封已标注邮件）。用几行话说明：模型是什么、参数怎么估计、对某类训练邮件里没出现过的词怎么办、怎样保证计算数值安全、以及一个要留意的弱点。

key_points.en: Model: P(y) times product of P(word | y); choose the largest
key_points.zh: Model: P(y) times product of P(word | y); choose the largest

key_points.en: Estimate by counting (relative frequencies per class)
key_points.zh: Estimate by counting (relative frequencies per class)

key_points.en: Sum of log probabilities to avoid underflow
key_points.zh: Sum of log probabilities to avoid underflow

key_points.en: Weakness: conditional independence, correlated words, over-confident probabilities
key_points.zh: Weakness: conditional independence, correlated words, over-confident probabilities

model_answer.en: Model: predict the class y that maximises P(y) multiplied by the product over the words of P(word | y), assuming words are conditionally independent given the class. Estimate P(y) as the fraction of emails in each class and P(word | y) as the relative frequency of the word among the emails of class y. Use add-one (Laplace) smoothing so a word unseen in one class does not make its probability zero. Add log probabilities instead of multiplying, to avoid underflow with thousands of small numbers. Weakness: words are correlated, so evidence is double counted and the probabilities are over-confident; the class decision is usually still fine.

title.en: What to remember
title.zh: 要记住的

blocks.tex: \hat y = \arg\max_{y} P(y)\prod_{m=1}^{F} P(x_m \mid y) = \arg\max_y \Big[\log P(y) + \sum_m \log P(x_m \mid y)\Big]

items.en: **Derivation:** $\arg\max P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$ $\to$ Bayes' rule $\to$ drop $P(\mathbf{x})$ $\to$ conditional independence (the only approximation).
items.zh: **推导：**$\arg\max P(y \mid \mathbf{x})$ $\to$ 贝叶斯公式 $\to$ 去掉 $P(\mathbf{x})$ $\to$ 条件独立（唯一的近似）。

items.en: **Training:** priors and likelihoods by counting = maximum likelihood. Gaussian: per class mean and standard deviation.
items.zh: **训练：**先验和似然靠计数 = 最大似然。高斯：每类的均值和标准差。

items.en: **Zero counts:** $\varepsilon$-smoothing (fewest $\varepsilon$'s wins, $\varepsilon \ll 1/N$) or add-$\alpha$: $\frac{\text{count} + \alpha}{n(y) + \alpha V}$. Laplace = MAP with a Dirichlet prior. More bias, less variance.
items.zh: **零计数：**ε 平滑（ε 最少的赢，$\varepsilon \ll 1/N$）或加 $\alpha$：$\frac{\text{count} + \alpha}{n(y) + \alpha V}$。拉普拉斯 = 狄利克雷先验下的 MAP。偏差更大、方差更小。

items.en: **Logs:** sum of log probabilities against underflow; the largest log score wins.
items.zh: **对数：**用对数概率求和防下溢；对数分数最大的赢。

items.en: **Linear:** for binary features the log-odds is $b + \sum w_m x_m$, the form of logistic regression; fitted by counting instead.
items.zh: **线性：**二值特征的对数几率是 $b + \sum w_m x_m$，与逻辑回归同形，只是用计数而不是优化来拟合。

items.en: **Works anyway** because only the argmax matters; **but** probabilities are over-confident when features are correlated.
items.zh: **仍然管用**，因为只有 argmax 重要；**但**特征相关时概率会过度自信。

items.en: **Generative:** models $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$; handles missing values by dropping factors.
items.zh: **生成式：**建模 $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$；缺失值靠去掉对应因子处理。
